definition: A formal request from a user for something to be provided — for example, a request for information, advice, or access to an IT service.
A structured database or module containing information about all live service offerings available to internal employees.
The authenticated employee or user who initiates and submits a service request ticket into the platform.
The operational team member assigned to process, work on, and resolve service requests within a specific department.
Manager level user responsible for overseeing ticket queues, reassigning workloads, and approving high-impact changes.
Administrative persona possessing elevated permissions to manage catalog forms, global SLA timers, and access controls.
Automated routing process that places incoming tickets into designated departmental work queues based on rules.
The single designated Fulfillment Agent currently assigned primary responsibility for bringing a ticket to resolution.
Documented commitment defining target operational response and resolution timeframe metrics for ticket fulfillment.
Key performance metric calculating the average time elapsed from ticket submission to state transition to RESOLVED.
Automated governance sequence requiring management sign-off before financial or high-risk requests can proceed.
Emergency management action allowing designated operational leads to bypass stalled approval gates.
Strict lifecycle model dictating allowed status transitions (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED).
An unsubmitted ticket saved locally by a requester prior to formal submission into the operational queue.
Immutable system record keeping historical logs of all ticket modifications, approvals, status changes, and overrides.
Group inventory of pending and active tickets categorized by service domain (e.g. IT Helpdesk, HR Operations).
Standardized knowledge base entry detailing steps to resolve specific common operational requests.
Frontline ingress server responsible for validating HTTP headers, security payloads, and file upload size caps.
Ticket state indicating work is paused while awaiting additional input or attachments from the original requester.
Automated HTTP callback pushing real-time ticket state events to external third-party software applications.
